title: Hide the password field when the password is being processed
line: The lock screen now empties the password field as soon as you submit it, so the password's length isn't shown while it's being checked.
explanation: MainBlock.startLogin() only moved focus to the unlock button and handed the password to PAM, so the field kept its dots until the check finished; it was cleared only on failure (clearPassword). On slow systems or slow PAM modules that shows the password's length for seconds. startLogin() now empties the field right after reading the password and restores its binding to PasswordSync, which also clears the copy on other screens, the same way clearPassword does.

commits.message:
lockscreen: clear the password field once unlocking starts

The typed password stayed in the field as dots while it was being
checked, which on slow systems shows its length to anyone nearby for
seconds. Now the field is emptied as soon as the password is submitted.

BUG: 455670

With the fix, same moment: the field is empty (placeholder) while the password is checked

review.text: Clearing passwordBox.text on submit while leaving the field visible and enabled-looking is a workaround with poor UX and does not actually hide the password field while authenticating as requested. During slow PAM checks it looks like the typed password was wiped into an empty input box with no busy/processing feedback (while focus stays on loginButton so typing does nothing and pressing Enter re-submits an empty password), on normal fast systems it flashes the empty placeholder on every unlock, and emptying the field breaks LockScreenUi's blockUI check so the 10 s fadeout timer can hide the UI mid-check. Rather than working around kscreenlocker's missing authenticating state in QML, kscreenlocker itself should expose a reliable busy/authenticating state during respond() so the lock screen can properly hide or replace the password field with a busy indicator.
changes: Fix kscreenlocker's Authenticator (a KDE repo) so its busy/authenticating property stays true while PAM is processing a respond() call until the next prompt, failure, or unlock.

In plasma-desktop's MainBlock.qml and LockScreenUi.qml, bind to that authenticating state to actually hide the password input row (or replace it with a busy indicator) while checking, clear/reset showPassword appropriately, and keep blockUI true while authenticating so the 10 s fadeout timer does not dismiss the UI during slow PAM checks.
